Buying an original painting online: a collector’s checklist

November 13, 2026

The image may be what draws you in. The details help you decide whether the painting belongs in your home. Use this checklist before you purchase an original artwork online.

1. Confirm exactly what you are buying

Look for the artist’s name, title, medium and support. An oil painting on canvas, a watercolor on paper and a printed reproduction are different objects. Check whether the listing is the unique original, an edition or a print. On Kimberly Marnell’s original-art collection, each featured work links to its own details and buying route.

Flourish, for example, is a 14 × 11 inch original oil painting from 2023. A print of a painting is a separate product: it lets you enjoy the image at another size or price, but it does not become the original. The original versus print guide explains that choice.

2. Measure the artwork and allow for the frame

Write down height and width, then mark that rectangle on your wall with paper or removable tape. Include the planned frame in the final outside measurements. Ask whether the listed dimensions describe the artwork, image, paper or framed object. A screen photograph does not establish how large the piece will feel above a sofa or near a doorway.

Kimberly’s featured direct originals are offered unframed. Think about the artwork’s support before choosing a presentation: paper and canvas need different framing decisions. Ask for clarification rather than assuming a frame shown in a room illustration is included.

3. Read the buying and delivery details

Confirm the current price and availability on the artwork page. Check what shipping is included, where the work can be delivered and which merchant will appear at checkout. Direct original-art purchases on this site disclose Haven Industries LLC as the checkout merchant; the artist brand remains Kimberly Marnell Art.

Read the returns and damage policy before paying. Direct original artworks are final sale for change of mind. Delivery problems and damage have their own reporting process. Marketplace prints use the marketplace’s ordering and return terms, which can differ from the direct-original policy.

4. Ask the question that would change your decision

If you need a closer view, clarification about a surface or delivery information, ask before purchasing. Name the artwork and explain what you need to know. A specific question is easier to answer than a general request for the whole catalogue.

You can email Kimberly about an original painting. If you need a different subject or size, the commission form provides a starting point for a personal painting. Confirm the project scope and timing before treating a request as an accepted commission.

5. Choose through the established sales route

Use the purchase or inquiry link provided for the work you have selected. Keep the title, dimensions and order confirmation with your records. You can enjoy choosing an artwork while still checking the practical details that make the purchase clear.
